Explain why a model is infeasible

Source: R/infeasibility.R
opt_explain_infeasibility.Rd

Solves an elastic relaxation of the model: every constraint row gets nonnegative slack variables that let it move toward feasibility, and with bounds = TRUE the bounds of continuous and integer variables do too. The relaxation minimizes the weighted total (L1) violation, so its solution names rows and bounds that can move, and by how much, for the model to become feasible at the least weighted total change. This is not the smallest number of rows to change, nor an irreducible infeasible subset: two copies of x >= 1 against one 100 * x <= 0 relax the two copies (total change 2) although relaxing the single upper row would suffice (change 100). Special constraints (indicators and SOS), binary bounds and integrality are kept as they are.

Usage

opt_explain_infeasibility(
  model,
  bounds = TRUE,
  weights = NULL,
  solver = "auto",
  ...,
  tol = 1e-07
)

Arguments

model

An opt_model().

bounds

Also relax variable bounds.

weights

Optional named numeric vector of weights by constraint block name (and ".bounds" for variable bounds); the default weight is

  1. A larger weight makes moving that block less attractive.

solver, ...

Passed to opt_solve() for the relaxation.

tol

Violations at or below tol are reported as zero.

Value

An opt_infeasibility list with feasible (whether the model is feasible, that is, no unweighted violation above tol is needed; the weights do not change this verdict), total (the weighted sum of violations), violation (their unweighted sum), violations, a data frame with columns kind ("row" or "bound"), name, block, side ("lower" or "upper"), bound (the original bound), value (the row or variable value at the relaxed solution) and violation, and result, the opt_solve() result of the relaxation.

Details

The model itself is not changed; the relaxation is built on a copy (see opt_copy()). For nonlinear models the relaxation is solved by a local solver unless the model is proven convex, so the explanation is then a local one.

Examples

m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = 2, lower = 0)
opt_constraint(m, x[1] + x[2] <= 1, name = "capacity")
opt_constraint(m, x[1] >= 2, name = "demand_1")
opt_constraint(m, x[2] >= 0.5, name = "demand_2")
opt_explain_infeasibility(m)
#> <opt_infeasibility: 1 row(s) and 0 bound(s) must move, total violation 1.5>
#>   row demand_1: lower bound 2, relaxed value 0.5 (violation 1.5)
